# CI: Designer boss wears a real creature model (2026-10-15)

Branch `feature/cyrus-boss-model`, commit 04674c3a (one commit on main 98d82fe0), worktree /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-boss-model.
Verified, NOT merged, NOT deployed. New switch `MB_BOSS_MODEL` (build service), default OFF.

## Problem (rc13 finding)
The designer route compiles the whole plugin from designs, and a boss design only names a vanilla `entity`. Nothing
could attach a BetterModel model, so rc13 switched the creature lane off up front and reported a lane gap. A prompt like
"a boss mob, the Hollow King, that summons minions" got a plain wither skeleton.

## What was built
1. **Spec (additive to designer schema v1).** On a boss: `"model": {"rig": "<creature name>", "scale"?: 0.5-2 (hard 0.25-4),
   "clips"?: {"attack"|"hurt"|"phase"|"death": "<clip>"}, "sounds"?: {"hurt"|"death"|"attack"|"ambient"|"spawn": "<key>"}}`.
   Minions can carry `summon.rig`, and encounter waves can carry `spawns[].rig` (with `entity` only; `rig_on_boss` is an
   error). The same zod source feeds the TS validator, the generated service checker (`designer-spec.js`) and
   `boss.v1.schema.json`.
   Cross-reference checks: a rig the mod does not have is the warning `rig_unresolved`, and the mob keeps its vanilla body
   (warn, don't block). Without a rig list the warning is `rig_unchecked`. Model sounds go through the normal boss sound
   checks (namespace, asset exists). Non-standard clips give `clip_custom`, and display equipment on a model boss gives
   `model_equipment`.
2. **Compiler.** `designer/BossModels.java` is emitted only when something wears a rig. It is the single class that uses
   `kr.toxicity.model.api`. It only calls members that javap shows in BOTH BetterModel 2.2.0 and 3.5.0: `modelOrNull`,
   `getOrCreate(BukkitAdapter.adapt)`, `scaler(ModelScaler.value)`, `animate`, `isClosed`, `close` and `damageTint`.
   - **Spawn:** the base mob is made silent and invisible before it enters the world, then the tracker is attached.
   - **Hitbox:** the scale attribute is set to rig hitbox height × model scale / vanilla height. This is computed at
     compile time.
   - **Clips:** BetterModel plays idle and walk by itself (its built-in tracker animations). The boss runtime plays the
     attack clip on every cast, the phase clip (default: the attack clip) on a phase change, and hurt (+ tint) and death
     clips. The model closes 3 s after death.
   - **Sounds:** the creature's sounds play on spawn, attack, hurt, death, plus ambient every 8 s.
   - **Cleanup:** models close on despawn, death, chunk unload (a sweep every AI tick) and disable. `/bettermodel reload`
     re-attaches lazily.
   - **Kept from the design:** boss bar, phases and abilities are unchanged.
   - **Declarations:** `depend: [BetterModel]` and the version's compile-only API deps (`bettermodel-api-2` /
     `-bukkit-api-2` on 1.21.x, `bettermodel-api` / `-bukkit-api` on 26.x) are added automatically.
   - **Evidence:** the mob gets the tag `<ns>.model`. `boss status` / `spawn` print
     `model <key> attached, hitbox xN, clips N (missing N), invisible true, silent true`, or
     `vanilla body (<why>), invisible false, silent false`.
   - **Boss mods without a model:** no BetterModel reference anywhere (the hub hooks stay dormant). Their golden hashes
     changed only because of the shared hub source.
3. **Planner / lanes (service).**
   - `parseAssetsRequest` keeps the creature lane next to the designer's bosses part when `MB_BOSS_MODEL=1`
     (`assets.bossModel`). Items- or menus-only designer builds still drop it, as in rc13, and with the switch off it is
     exactly rc13.
   - The design compile gets the workspace's valid rigs and their hitbox heights (`designs.js rigsOf`). The summary carries
     `rigsApplied` / `rigHeights`, and the portal re-compile passes them back, so `serviceAgreed` holds (tested).
   - On the designer route the creature soft checks talk about the design ("add "model":{"rig":...}").
   - `lanegaps`: a creature counts as delivered when something wears it. A creature that nothing wears is a gap with that
     reason.
4. **Prompt.** One line (505 chars, about 126 tokens) is inserted after the BOSSES section. It appears only when design,
   bosses, creature and bossModel are all on; otherwise the system prompt is byte-identical (tested). The user-turn
   creature hint changes to `a boss wears one with "model":{"rig":"<name>"}` (shorter). `BOSS_MODEL_PROMPT_VERSION =
   mb-bossmodel-2026-10-15.1`. The golden example is the Hollow King mod in `test/fixtures/cyrus-boss-model`:
   - a wither skeleton boss wearing the humanoid rig `hollow_king`, with a custom phase clip and four sounds;
   - zombie minions wearing the `hollow_thrall` ghost rig;
   - an encounter with thrall waves and then the boss.
   `scripts/cyrus/boss-model-golden.ts` regenerates it.
5. **Oracle.** For a boss that wears a creature of the build, when BetterModel is in the flight, `boss_spawns` adds two
   probes: the `<ns>.model` tag selector and `boss status` = `model <ns>_<rig> attached`. `creature_spawns` for that rig
   says it is proven by the boss's probes, and that its look still needs a client.

## Verification
- `tsc` reports 0 errors (devhost).
- Full `test/cyrus*` + `test/modbuilder*` suite: **4017 tests, 4016 pass, 1 fail**. The failure is the known pre-existing
  `cyrus-liveassets-e2e` "mid-stream views" timing failure.
- New `test/cyrus-boss-model.test.ts` (19 tests). Boss, HUD and docs goldens and references regenerated.
- **Real javac (node-2, `test/cyrus-boss-model-real.ts`):** 0 warnings and the strict scan is clean (0 blocks / 0 warnings)
  on both lanes:
  - 1.21.11 / JDK 21 against Paper 1.21.11 + the BetterModel 2.2.0 API;
  - 26.2 / JDK 25 against Paper 26.2 + the BetterModel 3.5.0 API.
  The API jars were fetched on node-2 from Maven Central and matched against the `deps.json` sha256. The fallback build
  compiles WITHOUT the API on the classpath. The existing boss fixtures still javac clean on both lanes.
- **REAL Test Flight A** (node-2, build lock held; Paper 1.21.11 + pinned BetterModel 2.2.0 paper jar, seeded libraries,
  the managed config and the two `.bbmodel` files Nxeon compiles from the rigs): **PASSED**, 7 checks, boot 19.5 s,
  peak RSS 1000 MB.
  - Both plugins enabled.
  - The spawn reply says `model nx_b0ssm0de_hollow_king attached`.
  - The `<ns>.model` tag is on the boss, `Silent 1b`, and the status shows `invisible true, silent true`.
  - Scale attribute is **1.21** (2.9 / 2.4); the minions wear their model at **0.82**.
  - BetterModel started the clips with **0 missing** (2 after hurt + cast, 4 after the phase change).

cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-content && cat > docs/cyrus/20-content.md <<'EOF'
# 20 Content engine (games, mods, spotlight, host, blog)

Branch `feature/cyrus-content` (2026-10-15, from main plus `feature/cyrus-community`). Additive; **nothing is deployed, applied or published**. Every public surface is behind a switch and off. Code: `lib/cyrus-site/*`, `app/(cyrus-web)/cyrus-web/**`, `components/cyrus/web/*`, `app/api/cyrus/spotlight`, `app/admin/cyrus/spotlight`. Tests: `test/cyrus-content.test.ts`. Plan and rollout: `agent-notes/cyrus-research/DB-cyrus-marketing-roadmap-2026-10-15.md` (section "Content, spotlight and hosting cross-sell") and the report `DC-content-engine-2026-10-15.md`.

## The honesty rule, and what was refused

The brief asked for artificially inflated views and ratings, invented users and invented authors on the public pages. **Not built**, on purpose: fabricated ratings, reviews and counters are deceptive, a legal risk for commercial promotion in many places (FTC fake-review rule and equivalents) and forbidden by this repo's own rule ("Never fabricate", `/opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md`). The honest equivalent that **was** built:

1. **Real counters** (views, installs, ratings) that start at zero. A page shows "New" until a count is real. No number is seeded, boosted or estimated anywhere (`lib/cyrus-site/views.ts`, `spotlight.ts`; tests pin it).
2. **Editorial curation**: "Staff picks" and "Mod of the week" chosen in the admin (Spotlight tool): reason line, order, start/end dates. The spotlight is never empty because staff fill it, and it is labelled for what it is. Real signals may blend in later ("Popular right now"), only past a minimum sample and only as a separate section.
3. **Seed content is real**: mods Cyrus actually built (owner batch, dungeon builds) published under one clearly labelled official author ("Made by the Cyrus team", staff badge). Never personas.
4. **Share-ready pages** so real creators can appear (author tag, canonical, JSON-LD, install button).

| Public path | Internal | Gate | Indexable when |

# Nxeon roadmap

Continuous-improvement backlog, highest priority first. Agents: pick the top unchecked item you can
complete end-to-end in one session, implement it, test it (build + E2E where relevant), commit, check
it off with a dated note, then stop. Add newly discovered work as new items rather than expanding
scope mid-task. **Every change must also update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit** (see
`CLAUDE.md` → "Documentation — keep it current") and run `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` if the doc
changed.

> Rewritten 2026-07-23 to reflect reality (the previous version had many shipped items still

### 4.1 Launch sequence (waves)

| Wave | When | Size (proposal) | Who | Gate to proceed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W0 private alpha | Weeks 1 to 3 | 25 | Hand-picked: Nxeon Minecraft server owners (paid and the free-MC owners who woke a server), 8 to 10 creators from the CSV (10K to 100K subscribers), a few hobby devs | See gates below |
| W1 | Weeks 4 to 5 | +100 | Waitlist, ordered by fit (has a server, answered "what do you want to build") | Same |
| W2 | Weeks 6 to 8 | +300 | Waitlist plus W0/W1 referrals | Same, plus cost per active user within cap |
| W3 | Weeks 9 to 11 | +1,000 | Waitlist, creator codes live | Plus moderation and report queue working |
| Public | Weeks 12 to 13 (target Jan 12 to 14) | open | Everyone | All launch gates (6.4) |

Wave gates (proposal, no benchmark exists; revise after W0):
- Median time from signup to first Test-Flight-passed build under 30 minutes.
- At least 50% of invited signups start a first build within 48 hours; at least 60% of first builds pass without a human fix.
- At least 40% of passed builds are installed on a server within 24 hours.
- Support load: median first response under 12 hours with the person available.
- Spend: average AI cost per activated user under the cap set from the plan price (price UNKNOWN, owner).

### 4.2 Week by week

| Wk | Dates | Product / growth work | Content / SEO | Community / creators | Owner vs agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Oct 19 | Promote CR SEO, CP community, CS Google login, CT legal after review; verify GSC (DNS TXT), Bing import, IndexNow, `www` 301 | Home head (canonical, OG, JSON-LD) live; capture week-1 baseline | Choose W0 list | Owner: promote, DNS, decisions. Agent: verify, runbooks |
| 2 | Oct 26 | Waitlist (email, double opt-in, "what will you build", server type: Nxeon / elsewhere / none, "how did you hear"), position and share link; invite mechanism with codes; event instrumentation (4.8); paid baseline eval | Plain "what Cyrus can and cannot do" page and `llms.txt` for cyrus.my | Send W0 invites after owner preview | Agent builds; owner approves copy and eval spend |
| 3 | Nov 2 | Activation emails (4.7) on shell v2; `CYRUS_NOTIFY` on; "invite a friend to join" card after install; cost screen honest (calibrated estimates, BL/BM) | Complete the Infinite Dungeon staged run (owner raises daily cap); capture screen recordings of 3 hero builds | W0 feedback calls (15 min each) | Owner records and runs calls |
| 4 | Nov 9 | W1 invites (+100); /admin/conversion Cyrus panel; weekly review starts | Use-case pages 1 to 3 (custom weapon, boss, GUI shop) with real prompts and outputs (CQ) | Seed 5 creators (free access, no obligation) | Agent drafts; owner approves claims |
| 5 | Nov 16 | Fix top 3 drop-offs found in W0/W1 data | Use-case 4 to 6; guide G1 (custom boss) | Discord section opened (needs community guild, E1 decisions) | Owner decides D1 to D6 |
| 6 | Nov 23 | W2 starts (+300); referral loop v1 behind flag (4.6) | Guide G2 (100-floor dungeon plugin) if the real build passes | First "mod of the week" spotlight | Owner picks spotlight; agent produces page |
| 7 | Nov 30 | Mod pages public for invited users only (gated flags); report and ban flow verified | Use-case 7 to 8; comparison page (honest, facts only) | Creator programme v1 live (4.4) | Owner signs creator terms |
| 8 | Dec 7 | W2 review; decide W3 | Guide G3 (plugin without coding); Cyrus entries on AlternativeTo (prepare) | Monthly build-off #1 announced | Owner runs contest rules past legal check |
| 9 | Dec 14 | W3 starts (+1,000); paid tests begin (4.9) | Use-case 9 to 10; G4 (quests) | Creator integrations scheduled for Jan | |
| 10 | Dec 21 | Holiday freeze on risky deploys; monitoring only | Build-off results, spotlight | | Owner: pause |
| 11 | Dec 28 | Public-readiness review against gates (6.4) | G5 (install on a server, backups, rollback) | Creator videos publishing | Owner decides go / no-go |
| 12 | Jan 4 | Public opening prep; Show HN prep (needs a no-signup try path or accept that HN is not for this stage) | Press kit, changelog | | Owner decides launch day |
| 13 | Jan 11 to 17 | Public launch; Show HN (only if tryable), Product Hunt, AlternativeTo, creator wave, Discord event | Launch post: build log, numbers from waves (real) | | |

### 4.3 Content calendar tie-in with the SEO plan

Follow CQ section 7 (use-cases 1 to 10, guides G1 to G5) but gate each page on a reproducible build. Add: (a) the dungeon and goblin case files as the two anchor pages; (b) a "what Cyrus cannot do" page (limits as a trust and GEO asset); (c) a monthly "what we got wrong" post; (d) the prompt library once there are 50 opt-in passing prompts. Cadence: about 2 pages a week, never a batch drop. Measure with CQ section 8 
### 4.5 Community plan (Discord, showcase, contests, spotlight)

- Discord: use the separate community guild approach from the Nxeon blueprint (support tickets must not share space with public chat). Cyrus channels: showcase, prompts-that-worked, fails-and-fixes, requests, changelog, help. Staff-run only until W2. Listing sites only after it has real members.
- Showcase: a post needs a join address or a clip of the mod working. Spotlight "mod of the week" = a curated page (existing `cyrus_featured_pages` and featured API), picked by the owner from public mods that pass Test Flight, have a screenshot or clip, and an author tag.
- Contests (monthly build-off): skill contest, theme set in advance, judged on a stated rubric, prize in tokens and a hosted-server month (cheap marginal cost) plus spotlight. Legal checks: official rules, no-purchase-necessary, age floor, taxes, and not implying Mojang endorsement.
- Do not copy a credit-for-activity Discord economy (player.games, vendor claim): it invites farming and costs real AI money per token.

### 4.6 Referral loop (tokens for invites, with safeguards)

Design: invite link per user from the post-install screen ("send this to the friend who will join") and from the mod page. Reward both sides in tokens when the invitee's first build passes Test Flight and is installed on a server. Safeguards: verified email only; reuse `starterEligibility` (blocks throwaway domains, normalises alias addresses and plus-tags); idempotency keys in the token ledger; monthly cap per refer

### 4.7 Email lifecycle (use the shared shell and tracking)

## 9. Content, spotlight and hosting cross-sell (appended 2026-10-15 by the content-engine agent; code on `feature/cyrus-content`, design in `docs/cyrus/20-content.md`, report `DC-content-engine-2026-10-15.md`)

**Scope.** The owner asked for blogs, a "best mods of the week" spotlight, game and mod pages, SEO, and Nxeon hosting cross-sell pages with a code and tokens. Everything below is BUILT behind switches (all off) and NOT deployed. One request was refused on purpose: artificially inflated views, ratings and invented authors. The honest equivalent (real counters that read "New", an editorial Staff pick and Mod of the week, real Cyrus-built seed mods under "Made by the Cyrus team") is what ships, and it fits section 4.5 of this plan (spotlight = curated, with a reason, from public mods that pass Test Flight).

### 9.1 Page inventory (cyrus.my)

| Page | Count at launch | Indexable when | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/games`, `/games/minecraft` | 2 | content public + indexing on | game hub; spotlight, categories, real captures, hosting CTA |
| `/games/<soon game>` | up to 6 | never (stub) | honest "coming soon", no dates |
| `/mods` | 1 | at least one mod passes the bar | This week, Staff picks, all mods, categories, search |
| `/mods/<slug>` | one per published mod (26 pages exist; 2 public today) | summary >= 120 chars, >= 1 command or feature, Test Flight not failed | the share-ready page: author tag, real counters, one-click install, honest status |
| `/host` | 1 | a Cyrus game with a plan and a location | hosting hub |
| `/host/<game>` | 1 per priced game (47 render; only Cyrus-live games index: Minecraft) | game is Cyrus-live or owner-allowed | "Minecraft server hosting" |
| `/host/<place>` | 1 per enabled node region (3 today: Singapore, Germany, Canada) | at least one indexable game | "Singapore game server hosting" |
| `/host/<game>/<place>` | game x place | indexable game | "Minecraft server hosting in Singapore"; today 3 indexable URLs, ~140 more render noindex |
| `/blog`, 5 posts, `/blog/rss.xml` | 7 | content public + indexing on | build logs and honest limits (supports the CQ guide plan) |

### 9.2 Templates

Three hosting layouts (showcase = a game, place = a location, compact = game in a location) plus the hub; one mod page layout; one post layout. Every template: Nxeon logo, a short hero on an original illustration (generated by `scripts/cyrus/web-art`), four true feature tiles, real plan cards (price per month from GamePlan), the discount block ONLY when the coupon exists, the token block ONLY when the economy is live and the scope covers the game, an FAQ built from visible facts, JSON-LD.

### 9.3 KPIs (all from GSC, the existing attribution tables and the new real counters; baselines are zero)

- Search: indexed vs submitted per section (core, mods, host, blog); impressions and clicks on host and blog URLs; non-brand queries in clusters E, H, I of the CQ plan; CTR on `/host/minecraft`.
- Funnel: page view -> "Install on my Nxeon server" click -> install; `/host` click -> deploy wizard -> paid order with `coupon=<code>`; tokens granted per server order (ledger `server_initial`).
- Spotlight: real views, installing accounts and ratings per picked mod vs unpicked (a causal-looking chart is NOT the claim; this is only to learn whether staff picks get seen).
- Quality: share of mod pages passing the bar; share of host URLs indexed; zero fabricated counters (a test, not a KPI).

### 9.4 Rollout order

1. Owner applies the one additive table, merges, deploys (staging, then promote). 2. nginx app-path list. 3. Seed the real mods and picks (dry run first). 4. Create the CYRUS coupon only if the owner decides the terms (otherwise the block stays hidden). 5. Open `cyrus_content_public_enabled` for the W0 private alpha (pages visible, noindex). 6. Week 6 plan item "first mod of the week": pick it in Admin > Cyrus > Spotlight. 7. At public launch: `cyrus_content_index_enabled`, `CYRUS_SITEMAP_CONTENT=1`, submit the sitemap, add Games / Mods / Host / Blog to the landing nav.

### 9.5 Risks

- A discount or token promise the system does not honour: mitigated by construction (the page prints only what the coupon row and the live token settings say); the open item is the owner's decision on the code's terms.
- Doorway pages: the host matrix can reach ~190 URLs; only Cyrus-live games are indexable (3 URLs today), cap 2,000, owner-extendable per game.
- Thin mod pages: quality bar; unpublished or failed-flight mods drop out of lists and the sitemap.
- Looking empty at launch: seed with REAL mods only; the honest empty states say what is missing. Do not "fix" emptiness with invented numbers (FTC fake-review rule and equivalents, and the repo rule).
- Views are page renders by non-bots, not unique visitors; labelled "views". No cookie or fingerprint is stored for counting.
- ccTLD `.my` geo signal and the nxeon.cloud canonical decision remain with the owner (CQ section 9).

- Funnel: page view -> "Install on my Nxeon server" click -> install; `/host` click -> deploy wizard -> paid order with `coupon=<code>`; tokens granted per server order (ledger `server_initial`).
- Spotlight: real views, installing accounts and ratings per picked mod vs unpicked (a causal-looking chart is NOT the claim; this is only to learn whether staff picks get seen).
- Quality: share of mod pages passing the bar; share of host URLs indexed; zero fabricated counters (a test, not a KPI).

### 9.4 Rollout order

1. Owner applies the one additive table, merges, deploys (staging, then promote). 2. nginx app-path list. 3. Seed the real mods and picks (dry run first). 4. Create the CYRUS coupon only if the owner decides the terms (otherwise the block stays hidden). 5. Open `cyrus_content_public_enabled` for the W0 private alpha (pages visible, noindex). 6. Week 6 plan item "first mod of the week": pick it in Admin > Cyrus > Spotlight. 7. At public launch: `cyrus_content_index_enabled`, `CYRUS_SITEMAP_CONTENT=1`, submit the sitemap, add Games / Mods / Host / Blog to the landing nav.

### 9.5 Risks

- A discount or token promise the system does not honour: mitigated by construction (the page prints only what the coupon row and the live token settings say); the open item is the owner's decision on the code's terms.
- Doorway pages: the host matrix can reach ~190 URLs; only Cyrus-live games are indexable (3 URLs today), cap 2,000, owner-extendable per game.
- Thin mod pages: quality bar; unpublished or failed-flight mods drop out of lists and the sitemap.
- Looking empty at launch: seed with REAL mods only; the honest empty states say what is missing. Do not "fix" emptiness with invented numbers (FTC fake-review rule and equivalents, and the repo rule).
- Views are page renders by non-bots, not unique visitors; labelled "views". No cookie or fingerprint is stored for counting.
- ccTLD `.my` geo signal and the nxeon.cloud canonical decision remain with the owner (CQ section 9).
EOF

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.content:
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
